---
title: "Phase Descent: Identifying Error Lineage in Passive Correlators from Harmonic Phase Coherence"
date: 2026-07-28
---

[Download PDF](../assets/phase-descent-calibration.pdf){.btn .btn-primary} &nbsp; [Source](https://github.com/TheChaosBureau/phase-descent-calibration)

## Abstract

Passive correlators recover signal overlap from the energy imbalance between
complementary interference channels — a physical realization of the
polarization identity. When the projections are phase-like, the output is
cosine in the angular difference between detector settings, and any distortion
generated by a single latent perturbation through a single nonlinearity
produces angular Fourier harmonics satisfying $\phi_n - n\phi_1 = 0 \pmod{\pi}$.

We call this property *phase descent*. It follows from the Chebyshev expansion
of analytic functions on $[-1,1]$, but is, to our knowledge, new as a
fault-lineage diagnostic. Phase descent partitions systematic errors into two
structurally distinct classes — analyzer asymmetry produces phase-locked odd
harmonics, while recombiner asymmetry produces phase-incoherent even harmonics
plus a DC offset — enabling a calibration diagnostic that extracts fault type,
fault severity, and its own validity bound from a single angular sweep.

Numerical experiments confirm phase-locking to within $10^{-4}$ rad for
analyzer errors up to 20% severity, while recombiner-induced inter-harmonic
phases drift continuously with error magnitude. The underlying principle
applies to any measurement architecture whose observable is well modeled as
$f(\cos(\theta - \theta_0))$.

## Scope

Numerical and SPICE-model results only; no instrument has been characterized
with the method. Built as a reproducible Quarto paper with a PySpice model
behind each figure.
